title: I Tried OpenClaw for a Month and I'm Never Going Back
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Nick says he has nothing to sell, then closes by mentioning Nick Consulting and a $5,000/hour rate that he says he probably should actually charge.

idea.name: On-demand custom printing
idea.one_liner: Print personalized designs on varied products for students, sports teams, and consumers, charging per order.
idea.customer: Students, school teams, runners, and consumers seeking customized products.
idea.offer: Print designs on demand on items such as shirts, shoes, tumblers, phone cases, banners, and stickers.
idea.revenue_model: Per-order sales are implied; prices are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: dude, you need to put this in your backpack, take it to school, plug it in, and print stuff on demand.
Just use this as your rapid testing machine and just learn where's the demand.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests that ten hours could be spent exploring possible ways to make money with the printer.
claims.quote: Like we could sit here for 10 hours and just scratch the surface of all the ways you could make money with this thing

acquisition_channels.details: Take the printer to school and offer on-demand printing while testing which products people want.

ideas.delivery: The operator brings and runs a physical printer at a school or other customer location, producing customized items on demand.

idea.name: Public company filings dashboard
idea.one_liner: A site that organizes public company filings and earnings data for people comparing companies.
idea.customer: People researching publicly traded companies, including executives and analysts.
idea.offer: A dashboard showing reporting dates, recent performance, revenue, themes, and analyst questions.

key_quotes.quote: I end up building this site where I can see when the next public reporting from these companies are, how they've done over the last quarter, where the revenue is, how they look.
I can go all the way and see just the themes, you know, how are things looking this quarter.

claims.claim: API Ninjas was offered at $20 per month for access to its APIs.
claims.quote: buy this $20 a month, you get access to all these other APIs.

ideas.delivery: A website dashboard populated with publicly available company filings and related data.

idea.offer: Configure an assistant with personal context, searchable records, and reminders across a user's information sources.
idea.revenue_model: Paid setup and support are suggested; amounts are not stated.

idea.name: Meeting capture and follow-up service
idea.one_liner: Record and transcribe company meetings, then make summaries, searchable records, and follow-up reminders available.
idea.customer: Individuals and companies that need to remember meeting decisions and commitments.
idea.offer: Meeting recording, transcription, summaries, searchable archiving, and accountability reminders.

key_quotes.quote: If you want to unlock the most value, record your meetings.
record a meeting, summarize it, put in a transcript, put it somewhere that you're going to check in

claims.claim: Nick uses an exaggerated example that following through on a meeting commitment could make millions of dollars.
claims.quote: that will make you millions of dollars

claims.claim: Nick says this practice puts users ahead of 95% of people, whom he says are not using it that way.
claims.quote: you're ahead of 95% of people because they're not using it for that right now.

ideas.delivery: A service records and transcribes meetings, creates summaries, stores searchable records, and prompts users about commitments and follow-ups.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Meeting recordings and transcripts may contain personal data; UK GDPR transparency, lawful processing, access control, and retention requirements are relevant.

idea.name: Company data cleaning and structuring
idea.one_liner: Help companies organize inconsistent files and data so AI systems can retrieve and use them.
idea.customer: Companies with large, fragmented document stores and inconsistent naming or taxonomy.
idea.offer: Clean, categorize, standardize, and structure business data for retrieval and AI use.
idea.revenue_model: Project or service fees are implied; amounts are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: helping companies get clean data is a multi-million dollar business.
you chunk it and you clean it and you tag it and you embed it whatever and then you set up these systems

claims.claim: Nick calls company data cleaning a multi-million-dollar business.
claims.quote: helping companies get clean data is a multi-million dollar business.

claims.claim: AI can do about 80% of cleanup, while the remaining 20% takes a long time.
claims.quote: You can get 80% of it done, but that last 20% takes a long time.

claims.claim: An AI process might categorize files to 80% confidence.
claims.quote: I could probably run AI on it and categorize everything to 80% confidence

claims.claim: The example company could still have 20,000 files that need manual decisions.
claims.quote: there's still, let's say, 20,000 files in there that you don't know where they go

ideas.delivery: A provider audits a company's data, automates initial categorization, resolves ambiguous files with staff, and structures the resulting collection for retrieval.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and appropriate security and processor arrangements are relevant where the data includes personal information.

idea.customer: Executives and leadership teams at companies, especially publicly traded companies.
idea.offer: Executive briefings, courses, weekly roundtables, AI consulting, fractional AI leadership, and ongoing briefings.
idea.revenue_model: Consulting and training fees are discussed; ongoing retainer or newsletter pricing is not stated.

idea.one_liner: Build small custom tools for organizations to reduce repetitive work and improve processes.
idea.customer: Organizations with manual workflows, inefficient meetings, spreadsheets, or dropped follow-ups.
idea.offer: Custom software and AI-powered tools tailored to specific company processes.

key_quotes.quote: The cost of custom code is so low that you can build customized tools that save people 80% of their time and it doesn't have to be like on the mass corporate scale.

claims.claim: Nick says custom tools can save people 80% of their time.
claims.quote: The cost of custom code is so low that you can build customized tools that save people 80% of their time

idea.name: AI search over company data
idea.one_liner: Give staff a natural-language interface for finding answers in an organization's proprietary data.
idea.customer: Organizations with proprietary data that staff cannot easily query.
idea.offer: An AI interface that lets employees search company data and ask operational questions in plain language.

key_quotes.quote: Probably the biggest unlock though is if you can figure out how to get proprietary data sets within an organization accessible to that organization.
If that would return an answer, that blows people's minds and you can do that right now.

ideas.delivery: A provider connects company data to an AI search interface and configures it to answer staff questions.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and appropriate access controls are relevant if connected company datasets contain personal information.

idea.name: Healthcare quality report access
idea.one_liner: Help healthcare organizations make quality reports available across all their locations.
idea.customer: Healthcare organizations that manage multiple provider locations.
idea.offer: Implement a way to retrieve and use quality reports across locations.

key_quotes.quote: Hey, I will show you how to get every single one of your quality reports for every one of your locations in the next 6 weeks.

claims.claim: Nick suggests implementing report access across locations within six weeks.
claims.quote: I will show you how to get every single one of your quality reports for every one of your locations in the next 6 weeks.
